# Mapping access to sanitation and safely managed drinking water across low- and middle-income countries

## Overview

Link to the repository:

This repository contains code for modelling subnational estimates of basic sanitation, open defecation, and safely managed drinking water (SMDW) across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), using household survey data and geospatial covariates. Models are trained at the survey region level and predictions are generated for all LMIC admin1 units.

The SMDW component extends methods developed in Greenwood et al. (2024), which produced the first subnational estimates of safely managed drinking water services across LMICs and extends this to apply deep learning models. We apply the modelling framework to basic sanitation coverage and open defecation and subcomponents of SMDW.

## Project folder overview

The repository is organised into the following top-level folders:

**`scripts/`** All analysis scripts, organised into four numbered subfolders that follow the pipeline from raw data to final outputs: data preparation (`01`), feature selection (`02`), model training (`03`), and additional analysis and visualisation (`04`). See [`scripts/README.qmd`](scripts/README.qmd) for a full description of each script.

**`data/`** Input data used by the pipeline, split into `raw/` (original source files) and `processed/` (files derived or prepared by scripts or manually). Not all data is stored in this repository — large files (household survey microdata, GEE-sampled covariates, country-level covariate tables, and deliverable outputs) are stored in a switchdrive folder. See [`data/README.md`](data/README.md) for a full inventory of the data, including switchdrive locations and original sources.

**`outputs/`** Final analysis outputs generated by the scripts. Organised by pipeline stage:

| Subfolder | Contents |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `cluster_analysis/` | Covariate cluster analysis results for feature selection |
| `model_performance/` | Model evaluation metrics, prediction files, and performance plots |
| `descriptive_statistics/` | Descriptive summaries of training data coverage and distributions |
| `main_figures/` | Main figures for manuscript |

**`functions/`** Shared R helper functions sourced by the data preparation scripts. Covers extraction and labelling of DHS and MICS survey variables for both sanitation and SMDW outcomes, country name harmonisation, dataframe joining utilities, and diagnostic helpers.

**`configuration/`** Project-level configuration files sourced by scripts at runtime:

| File | Contents |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `paths.R` | All switchdrive and external file paths — edit here when data moves |
| `covariate_cols.R` | Named vector of covariate column names used consistently across training and prediction |
| `manual_region_fixes.R` | Hand-coded region name corrections applied during the GADM crosswalk step |
| `country_name_key_WB.csv` | Lookup table of country name variants mapped to World Bank standard names |

## Getting started

## Setting up the project environment

This repository uses **`renv`** to manage R packages and **`venv`** to manage Python packages. Using both helps keep the computational environment reproducible across users and systems.

After cloning the repository, open the project from the repository root in **Positron** or **RStudio**. Restore the R environment with:

renv::restore()

Then create a Python virtual environment in the project directory: python -m venv .venv

Activate the environment and install the required Python packages from the dependency file used in this repository by running pip install -r requirements.txt.

In Positron or RStudio, make sure the interpreter is set to the project-specific Python environment and that R uses the restored renv library.
